name: Kingdom of France

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 390,000 km2 for 1350 and 1400 and 340,000 km2 for 1450 (low). The world_1400 France polygon measures 393,605 km2. High allows for Brittany and Burgundian lands counted as part of the kingdom.

population.note: Seshat codes 9.0 million (1400) and 9.5 million (1450); HYDE/OWID France 1400 = 10.9 million within modern borders (high side). Down from ~16-20 million before the Black Death.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Paris 200,000-300,000 (Seshat), Rouen, Lyon, Toulouse, Orleans.

activePersonnel.note: Troops in royal pay in October 1415: the army at Agincourt, 12,000 (Curry) or 14,000-15,000 (Rogers, Mortimer, Sumption: 10,000 men-at-arms + 4,000-5,000 gens de trait) plus up to 10,000 armed valets (high); plus garrisons of Normandy, Picardy and the Gascon march. Contingents of Brittany (6,000, Monstrelet), Anjou (600) and Brabant (2,000) were still marching and are not counted.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Arriere-ban of the nobility and town militias not yet summoned; Burgundian forces withheld by John the Fearless.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Royal artillery train, Clos des Galees crews at Rouen, heralds and officials.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. The noble class (40,000 noble families under the Valois, Seshat) plus militias.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Men-at-arms: 10,000 at Agincourt (herald of the Duke of Berry, via Rogers, Mortimer, Sumption; Curry 2000 p. 181) + ~3,000 in garrisons.

quality.note: Rubric 1.0: best plate harness in Europe.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: individually trained nobles, little collective drill.

count.note: 4,000-5,000 archers and crossbowmen at Agincourt + ~1,000 in garrisons.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: crossbows, slower than the longbow.

count.note: Educated guess. Pavisiers, town militia and armed valets fighting on foot (high includes part of the 10,000 gros valets).
Educated guess. Royal bombards and smaller guns; few reached Agincourt.
Educated guess. Royal galleys of the Clos des Galees at Rouen; France relied on hired Castilian and Genoese ships.
Educated guess. Balingers and coastal craft.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25: Charles VI insane, divided command at Agincourt where Constable d'Albret and Marshal Boucicaut were overruled by princes of the blood.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25: Armagnac-Burgundian civil war; Burgundy stood aside.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: confident in numbers, defending the homeland, but riven by faction.

weapons.note: Anchor 4 plus: crossbow, lance, poleaxe, bombards.

fortification.note: Anchor 4: walled towns and castles, Harfleur held five weeks.

logistics.note: Anchor 4: river transport (Seine, Loire), local supply.

isr.note: Anchor 4 minus: shadowed the English march but misjudged numbers.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Wartime: taille and aides for the 1415 army; low = peacetime share.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Post-plague land abundance, disrupted by war.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Royal roads and surviving Roman routes.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Rouen, Harfleur, Dieppe, La Rochelle, Nantes (Breton), Marseille (Provence, outside the kingdom), Aigues-Mortes, Narbonne.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Atlantic and Channel coastal trade.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and oxen, ~0.2-0.3 per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: walled towns and familiar terrain; civil war limits population support.

notes: Snapshot = October 1415, the Agincourt campaign. Agincourt numbers are disputed: Curry's record-based 12,000 French vs 9,000 English, against Rogers, Mortimer and Sumption's ~14,000-15,000 French (plus up to 10,000 valets) vs ~6,000 English (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt). The 1415 royal army was largely paid men-at-arms in companies and counts as activePersonnel at the date; the unsummoned arriere-ban is trainedReserves. Population convention: the kingdom per Seshat, including Burgundian and Breton fiefs held under the crown; English Gascony and Calais excluded. Same nationId as later france snapshots.
